name: Nuratau-Kyzylkum Biosphere Reserve
blurb: Wild sheep, vultures and almond groves where the Nuratau range meets the desert.

sources.title: Uzbekistan government: The Nurata State Reserve

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: A wild mountain sheep. The Nuratau-Kyzylkum reserve is said to hold the only wild population of the Severtsov subspecies. Wikipedia names wolves as the main argali predators.
An omnivore that roots for plant foods, nuts and small animals. Listed among the mammals of the Nurata reserve.
A hare of Central Asian steppe and desert that eats grasses and herbs. It is common prey for foxes and buzzards.
A rocky-slope game bird that eats seeds, leaves and some insects. Well recorded in the reserve area, and prey for eagles, buzzards and foxes.
An adaptable predator and scavenger. GloBI records it eating many of the birds, hares and lizards of the area.
A cliff-nesting vulture that feeds on carcasses of large animals. It is listed in the Uzbekistan Red Data Book as a breeder in the range.
A huge vulture that eats mainly carrion, including carcasses of wild sheep and domestic livestock. Globally threatened, and it breeds in the Nuratau range.
Listed among the mammals of the Nurata reserve. Wikipedia names wolves as the main predators of argali, especially in hard winters.
A raptor of open dry steppe and rocky country. It takes ground squirrels, hares, lizards and chukars, and nests on cliffs.
Long, hot, dry summers drive the desert and foothill plants.

nodes.name: Soil microbes & beetles
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, dung and carcasses and return nutrients to the thin dry soil.
